The new standard for email security
There’s a new standard in AI-powered email security, and it’s Sublime | IVP

The 360 billion emails that cross the internet each day are a risky vector for cyber attacks, now costing businesses upward of [$3 billion annually](https://www.ic3.gov/AnnualReport/Reports/2023_IC3Report.pdf). Unchallenged, this problem will only get worse.

AI has given hackers the means to execute targeted phishing attacks on an unprecedented scale, while email security remains a conventional, slow, one-size-fits-all black box. Even the most advanced API-based email security vendors still leave their customers in the dark, with no ability to adapt their environment to the changing threat landscape without filing a ticket.

This is an industry ripe for disruption. We need software to keep up with attacker adaptation programmatically — that is, software running with minimal human input required, versus the other way around.

That’s why we’re leading Sublime Security’s $60 million Series B — to supercharge the email security revolution we’ve all been waiting for.

**A new programmatic method to email security in the AI era**

Sublime is solving these problems for its rapidly growing customer base with an approach that takes into account newly available technology: countering attackers with an adaptive AI detection engine. Sublime treats each customer as a unique organization with individual email security needs. By adapting the Sublime model to meet the discrete security needs of different segments of its workforce — sales, IT, C-suite, and so on — Sublime’s email security platform thwarts email threats more precisely and accurately.

**An expert founder who knows the enemy**

Sublime’s success has a lot to do with its founders, [Josh Kamdjou](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jkamdjou/) and [Ian Thiel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ianthiel). With a background in offensive security, including a decade of deep work for the U.S. Department of Defense, Josh understands how attackers operate - and how relatively easy hacking a network by phishing can be.

This "know your enemy" posture has been instrumental in developing Sublime's innovative defenses. Josh’s mission in building Sublime was to create a solution that he himself wouldn’t be able to subvert.

Ian brings operational strength to Josh’s security expertise, leveraging his product and GTM leadership roles at Optimizely and Alto Pharmacy to help commercialize and operationalize Sublime.

We’re impressed with their relentless drive to disrupt the email security status quo and their focus on solving the *problem* and not just pushing a solution.

**Fast growth, glowing customer reviews and huge addressable market**

Sublime’s growth has been rapid and organic, correlated to the unconstrained market – one denominated in the total number of business email addresses worldwide. Sublime serves customers like Spotify, Snyk, Elastic, Brex and Ramp, and has quadrupled its customers since the beginning of this year.

We believe this momentum is about to increase even further with the addition of former Wiz CRO Colin Jones as President. Colin brings a wealth of experience and a customer obsession. Customers rave about Sublime’s efficacy, ease of use and responsiveness. We look forward to more happy customers via Colin.

The combination of growth, expertise, customer love and market opportunity? Sublime.

As a partner to CEOs, I draw most on my time as a professional athlete and my experience in enterprise sales at Oracle and Cloudera. I started my career as a runner for Nike, competing on a global level for two years. As any athlete knows, professional or otherwise, every ounce of energy invested in preparation increases your competitive edge. If you’re targeted in training and tenacious enough to persevere, it translates on race day. In sport and in company-building, there’s no substitute for putting in the time and effort—no shortcut to success. 
 
In my role in venture, I think of being a partner to founders and execs in the same way that I think about being on a sports team: we all have one another’s best interests in mind, and we’re united through a shared understanding and a common goal. Both inside the walls of the firm and beyond them. 

I strive to go the extra mile for the companies I work with, leveraging my knowledge of enterprise sales to contribute in meaningful ways, whether by surfacing candidates for key roles, providing benchmarking and contextual data, making introductions or asking the right question at the right time.

From technology that enables cloud and data infrastructure to stacks emerging for AI or information security, I work with companies developing underlying infrastructures for autonomous and business applications and for consumer experiences. That means I get to live in the future every day, hearing founders talk about the reality they aspire to create and the gaping holes they see and seek to fill. Working together toward their vision and seeing it come to fruition is the sweetest victory of all.

You can immediately tell when you’re using a product that was created by founders with a clear understanding of the customer's needs and incredible passion. Well-crafted products reveal the founders and creators behind them through their novel and often non-obvious approach to solving a problem and attention to detail in that solution.

I’m energized by working with product visionaries, so I always knew that I wanted either to be a startup founder or invest alongside founders. After my start in investment banking and early-stage venture, I joined Drobo as head of product marketing—a role that deepened my empathy for founders and operators alike. Together, these experiences revealed that my heart was in venture—where my passion for technology and my passion for people intersect. If I can speak with customers and feel their passion for the product and company I’m evaluating, that gives me an incredible amount of energy and conviction. 

While I’m a generalist at heart, I gravitate toward companies with distinct, identifiable technological advantages. I’m compelled by understanding why now—what has shifted or changed in the world that allows this opportunity to exist at this specific moment in time. When that advantage is paired with a striking sense of urgency and determination from the founder, you get the feeling that together you can not only see the future but also shape it.

Startup founders are irrationally optimistic. They take on huge challenges, persist through rejection, and navigate extreme uncertainty. Without irrational optimism, their companies wouldn’t exist or stand a chance to succeed. As an investor, joining them in that optimism and reaching the point of unwavering belief in their vision is nothing short of a thrill. The real fulfillment, though, comes from partnering deeply with founders through the inevitable highs and lows of turning that vision into reality.

I grew up in South Florida and went on to study economics and play hockey at Tufts University. After college, I started my career in investment banking, learning more about financial modeling and analysis than I ever wanted to. I then spent a couple of years as a Series A investor, focusing on products, markets, and teams. Now at IVP, I bring together the quantitative skill set I built in banking and qualitative skill set I built in early-stage venture to guide founders and help IVP partner with outstanding companies.

There’s nothing quite as satisfying as sprinting toward an ambitious objective as a team. From my time in product to the work I do now at IVP, a critical part of my role has been identifying the highest-impact customer problems and partnering with those who feel an irrational compulsion to solve them.

Having worked across all the phases of a startup’s lifecycle, from pre-PMF to IPO, I strive to bring that context as I partner with the founders building the next generational companies. At Snowflake, I came to deeply appreciate the transformative power of applying step-function architectural improvements to universal workflows. My time at Confluent taught me that product and GTM are two sides of the same coin. And my experiences at early-stage startups left me with a deep appreciation for the process of finding product-market fit.

Across it all, I’ve internalized the mindset that opportunity comes down to having an open mind. Every meeting and interaction with founders is a chance to see the world from a different point of view and learn something new. It might sound simplistic or easy, but the willingness to listen, learn and believe is often the difference between spotting and missing the next big thing.
